body: Hit testing: a hit still stops at the padding box of every box that clips by overflow and reads own_x/own_y; upstream's content test enters in its new form, the point against the scrollable overflow rect's four sides plus the client offset, and an element with no computed styles yet can now be hit before the first resolve without a panic.
An inert element still takes no hit: the hit-testing inert promise must hold through the reworked hit path and the self match.

Element bounds the snapshot and the driver read: a scrolled box reads its own bounds where it stands with no subtraction of its own scroll offset, and absolute_position subtracts only its containing blocks' offsets, so a box's bounds, a closed select's option bounds, an open list's row bounds and a multiple select's row bounds read unchanged on the stand.

The driver's synthetic click lands at the node's centre computed from those bounds, and its covered refusal reads the hit at that point; both must read as before where the engine's readings do not change.

Scroll into view: escher's scroll_into_view brings a target into view through every scrolling box that holds it, now reading each box's scroll state as current, min and max and skipping a box whose min and max are both zero; a scroll range may run negative under reversed origins.

Shown scrollbars: the scrollbar band and thumb geometry moves onto the new scroll range, and a driver click in a shown scrollbar band still drags its thumb; the default thumbs' contrast stroke is unaffected in kind.

A node with no computed styles: the new scroll-container read must read false rather than panic, at each of its three call sites, so the select list test where a select made inert, disabled, hidden or removed with its list open closes the list passes under the workspace's features.
The open select list overlay and its rows keep one row height, their engine colours and their bounds through the layout change; the list's close on inert or removal keeps its focus behaviour.

No new carrier, verb, argument, result field, node key, cause, session error, exit, log field or span: the driver's answers, the snapshot and the accessibility tree change only where the engine's readings change, and the measurement reads none changed.

Upstream's scroll-shifted readings in physical_unrounded_geometry's second body and in hit_inner's self match must not enter; escher's own-scroll rule, its hit stop and its absolute_position reading are kept.

The take is read back, not re-measured: every leg measured green in the trial (fast, msrv, audit, doc, build, counter, wasm, a11y, stand-repeat three of three rounds), the a11y and stand-repeat tallies unmoved, the committed cross-OS stand digests and Counter checks passing unchanged; coverage and the WPT suites were not run, and the cross-OS digests read only linux locally.
The stand reads no lint finding at boot and its contrast assertions hold with the moved layout, since the lint's contrast finding carries bounds read from the same geometry.
No other upstream commit enters; the later upstream sync stays its own chunk.
Keyboard navigation contracts (range input keys, single-choice and multiple select keys, CRUD list and Cells grid keys, Tab order, keyboard activation): the take changes no key handling.
ARIA property reads, ARIA states, role mapping and accessible name precedence: no attribute read, role or name rule changes.
The platform accessibility adapter, the accessibility feature defaults and the AccessKit adapter's creation order: no feature, dependency or adapter wiring other than the Taffy rev moves.

body: Upstream changes are taken by cherry-pick: exactly these seven commits, in upstream order. No other upstream commit enters, and the later upstream sync stays a chunk of its own.

Taffy moves to a3997d55 under the no-git-dependencies invariant. Its Taffy exception stays as it is: still a git source pinned at a full commit rev, with no patch section, no checksum and no change to the dependency list. Cargo legs stay locked against the lockfile.
This take does the deferred Taffy bump past the ScrollableOverflow change, which used to leave blitz-dom uncompiled. The Stylo and Dioxus bumps stay deferred.

Upstream's behaviour change is ratified per take. The reversed-scroll-origin change applies to every document: a box's content is measured against Taffy's ScrollableOverflow rect, and its scroll range can run negative. It is taken as an engine behaviour change, on the founder's ratification for this take.

The scrolled-box bounds rule is kept: a scrolled box's client rect and bounds read the box where it stands, with no subtraction of its own scroll offset. Upstream's scroll-shifted reading in the physical geometry does not enter.

The hit stop at clipping padding boxes is kept: a hit stops at the padding box of every box that clips by overflow and reads that box's own offsets. Only the content test takes upstream's form: the point is checked against the scrollable overflow rect's four sides plus the client offset.
The absolute-position rule is kept: Node::absolute_position subtracts only its containing blocks' scroll offsets and never its own.

The into-view scroll still writes the whole containing-block chain and still writes nested boxes instantly. It now reads each box's scroll state as current, min and max, and skips a box whose min and max are both zero.

Upstream's fix enters: an element with no computed styles yet can be hit tested, including before the first resolve. Escher's own scroll-container check reads false for a node with no computed styles, so no overflow read panics when a select list is closed by making its select inert, disabled, hidden or removed.

Physical layout takes upstream's fourth argument, and placer geometry still subtracts each placer's scroll offset. The stylo_taffy exports and the Taffy traversal and layout traits follow the new Taffy: the CopyStyleGetters import is dropped.
The Stylo prefs stay as set once by Stylo 0.22 names. The document conflict resolves to escher's side, so upstream's sideways pref does not enter.
Scrollbar geometry shared by paint and hit test follows the new scroll range, a range that can run negative.

The driver boundary does not widen: no new carrier, verb, argument, result field, node key, refusal cause, session error, exit code, log field or span. The driver's answers change only where the engine's readings change, and the measured stand read none changed.
Stand readings must stay identical on every CI OS. The committed cross-OS digests and the committed stand Counter checks must pass unchanged.
The escher-side seam edits in blitz-dom are direct engine changes and are flagged upstreamable: the scroll-container check, the into-view scroll-state reading and the dropped import.

The take re-reads the earlier measurement and does not re-measure. The measurement found every leg green except coverage and the WPT suites, which were not run. The test tally rose from 1501 to 1510 with upstream's nine tests, and the a11y and stand-repeat tallies did not move. The stand-repeat budget is zero failures.
The WPT attribute tests read checkLayout attributes from layout geometry. That geometry now uses reversed scroll origins.
Upstream's tests ride the picks: a new blitz-tests integration target for inline-box scrollable overflow, and a blitz-dom unit test for hit testing before the first resolve.

body: The engine's Taffy pin moves to upstream's rev. Taffy stays a git source pinned at a full commit rev, with no patch section and no checksum, and the dependency list is unchanged. Taffy remains the one exception to the no-git-dependency rule, and the rev is the only thing that changes. The exception must stay as stated, together with the engine dependency pins and the rule that an upstream sync takes its dependency set whole.
The moved lockfile must pass the gates every push owes: locked builds, the MSRV leg, the cargo-deny advisory audit (where ignores are allowed only by ID, each with a reason) and the licence gate.

New behaviour for every document: a box's content is measured against Taffy's scrollable-overflow rect, and its scroll range can run negative. Programmatic scroll still clamps to that range and still ignores a missing node.

The hit test keeps escher's stop at the padding box of every box that clips by overflow, and its self match keeps reading the box's own position. The content test now takes upstream's form: the point is checked against the four sides of the scrollable-overflow rect plus the client offset. A non-invertible transform still takes no hit.

Hit testing an element that has no computed styles yet (upstream's #1304) must neither panic nor take the hit wrongly. This joins the rules that a never-styled node is not read as styled and that a stale node id never panics.

New private scroll-container read: it answers false for a node with no computed styles and is used at three layout sites. Without it, upstream's new overflow read panicked when an inert, disabled, hidden or removed select closed its open list. The engine must not panic on content the page supplies or on a node a call names.

Into-view scrolling reads the scroll state as current, min and max, and skips a box whose min and max are both zero. It brings a target into view through every scrolling box that holds it. That includes the open select list, which scrolls a row into view by the row's own offset.

The node's absolute position subtracts only its containing blocks' scroll offsets, and a scrolled box reads its own bounds without subtracting its own offset. The visible region read through transforms, the visible region of an open select list row, and the off-screen and covered refusals all rest on these readings.

Boundary held: no new carrier, verb, argument, result field, node key, refusal cause, session error, exit code, log field or span. The driver's answers change only where the engine's readings change, and the measurement found none changed on the stand.

Upstream's scroll-shifted readings in the second body of the physical geometry and in the hit test's self match do not enter. Escher's own-scroll rule and each placer's subtracted offset stay as they are.
No other upstream commit enters this take. The later upstream sync stays a chunk of its own.
The scrollbar geometry and its fade read the new scroll range. The fade still runs on the document clock, and time moves only on advance.
Inline-box sizes, now read with scrollable overflow, stay finite.
Re-read, not rebuilt: the committed cross-OS stand digests and the committed stand-Counter checks pass unchanged against the take.
The WPT runner's attribute test runner follows upstream. Its results stay within the runner's result kinds, and only JavaScript script types are treated as scripts.

body_fields.convention: A new test in the engine test crate takes no tracing and no style setup of its own, and the test crate stays unpublished.
A new engine unit test that hits or lays out a node before its styles resolve reads none or false rather than panicking.

body: The Taffy dependency moves to upstream's pin a3997d55. It stays a git source pinned at a full commit rev, with no patch section and no checksum, and the dependency list does not change. The Taffy exception to the no-git-dependency rule is kept as it stands; only the rev changes.

Reversed scroll origins for every document: a box's content is measured against Taffy's scrollable overflow rect, and its scroll range may run negative. This is a behaviour change, ratified for this take.

A scrolled box reads its own bounds where it stands, with none of its own scroll offset subtracted. Upstream's scroll-shifted reading in the box geometry reader does not enter. A placer's geometry still subtracts each placer's offset, and the box's physical layout takes upstream's fourth argument.

A hit stops at the padding box of every box that clips by overflow, and the self match reads the box's own x/y. Upstream's scroll-shifted self match does not enter. The content test takes upstream's form: the point is tested against the scrollable overflow rect's four sides plus the client offset.
A node's absolute position subtracts only its containing blocks' scroll offsets.

The into-view scroll brings a target into view through every scrolling box that holds it. It reads each box's scroll state as current, min and max, and skips a box whose min and max are both zero. Its reach is a harness input helper, scroll_into_view.

Hit testing an element that has no computed styles yet does not panic. A node with no computed styles is not a scroll container. This keeps the select popup's close-on-inert/disabled/hidden/removed check from panicking under the workspace's features.

Pointer clicks, the harness's click on a clipped element and the harness centre and layout-rect readings all hit test and read positions through the engine. They must keep the readings they had: the driver's answers change only where the engine's readings change, and the measurement found none changed on the stand.
The driver surface stays as it is: no new carrier, verb, argument, result field, node key, cause, session error, exit, log field or span.

Upstream's tests ride the picks: a new blitz-tests target for inline-box scrollable overflow, and an inline blitz-dom unit test of hit testing before the first resolve. The workspace test tally moves from 1501 to 1510, a rise of nine, each attributed by test name. The a11y and stand-repeat tallies do not move.
The cross-OS answer digests of the served tasks and the committed Counter checks pass unchanged. Linux x86_64 was read in the trial; windows and macOS are read only in CI.
The stand checks stay green over three stand-repeat rounds, with a zero-failure budget, in both layout modes.

The CI legs read green: fast, msrv (Rust 1.91, verified by build), audit (dependency advisories and licenses over the new Taffy rev), doc, build, counter, wasm, a11y and stand-repeat. Clippy runs over the workspace and upstream blitz-dom. The cargo legs run locked against the updated lockfile.
Only the seven named upstream commits enter, taken by cherry-pick in upstream order. No other upstream commit enters; the later upstream sync stays a chunk of its own.
Overlay scrollbar geometry follows the new scroll range. A container that has never been scrolled paints no scrollbar thumb.

body_fields.convention: each blitz-tests test file is its own test target, and the blitz-tests manifest keeps its stated difference from upstream
unit tests sit in an inline test module of their source file
blitz-dom fixtures are built without the HTML parser, and test data is stated in code
a layout assertion runs in both layout modes, and every layout reader word is read on a fixture
a move in a test tally is attributed by test name
